note: Hand-written inputs for the state machine in docs/WORKERS.md section 3. Several cases pin behaviour that browsers get right and hand-written parsers usually get wrong: a '>' inside a quoted attribute, an unclosed tag, a '<' that is not a tag, and entities without their semicolon. extract never normalizes, so newlines and spacing are preserved verbatim.

cases.note: baseline
block tags give newlines, inline tags do not
a > inside a quoted attribute must not close the tag
an unclosed tag at the end is dropped as a tag
a removed element without its closing tag runs to the end of the input
script, style, noscript, template, svg and iframe go with their content
comments and doctype go, CDATA keeps its text
CDATA is character data: what is inside it is literal text and must NOT be parsed as markup, so the tags survive
an unclosed CDATA section keeps everything to the end of the input, the same principle as a removed element with no closing tag

character data means character data: nothing inside a CDATA section is interpreted, so entities stay literal - the half of the rule an implementation still gets wrong after it stops treating tags as tags
removal wins over CDATA: a script element goes with its content, even when that content is character data

input ends right after a tag name: the incomplete tag is dropped and contributes no newline, so "<p" is the empty string (this is where the reference contradicted its own rule until the Python differential run found it)
a title inside an anchor belongs to the title and to nothing else: not to the body, not to the link's text
named with and without a semicolon, decimal, hex, unknown, and a name followed by digits
the first title wins and the title text is not part of text
the title is entity-decoded but not normalized
img tags are counted, and one inside a comment is already gone
relative, absolute, protocol-relative and schemeless with a port
the link's text keeps its inner tags dropped and its spacing verbatim
a < not followed by a letter, / or ! is literal text
each listed tag contributes a newline on open and on close
table/tr/th/td are newline tags
CJK passes through, the link text too
decodes to a space here, and the composition with normalize is a separate case in the harness
empty html is valid
everything removed leaves empty text, not null
a link with no href still produces an entry, with an empty href
nested anchors follow the browser: the outer is closed and reported when the inner opens, and the inner is still open at end of input, so both are reported
the same rule with the inner anchor properly closed: two links, each with its own text

input ends inside a tag: the incomplete tag is dropped including its name characters (a browser's eof-in-tag), so this is "\nabc" - the case that nothing in the corpus could see before, and where the reference and one implementation disagreed
a < with nothing after it is literal text (a browser's tag-open state), unlike the case above
